legend: Gross features of a follicular adenomatoid odontogenic tumour showing a thick fibrous capsule around the crown of a permanent premolar, with intraluminal proliferation.
Tumour showing prominent epithelial proliferation organized in solid nodules and strands formed by cuboidal odontogenic epithelial cells, with round arrays of back-to-back columnar cells.

Extrafollicular example. A fibrous capsule encloses odontogenic epithelium organized in solid nodules and strands of varying size containing duct-like structures and focal calcification in a haemorrhagic stroma.

Cropped panoramic radiograph showing an adenomatoid odontogenic tumour with cyst formation on the upper first premolar. The corticated radiolucency is associated with tooth root displacement. There is no visible internal mineralization.
source: Alexander Tadeu Sverzut - Oral Surgery FOP-UNICAMP, Brazil

legend: An extrafollicular adenomatoid odontogenic tumour demonstrating a fibrous capsule delimiting odontogenic epithelium organized in solid nodules and strands of varying size containing duct-like structures and focal calcification in a haemorrhagic stroma.
Submucosal cystic tumour showing odontogenic epithelium organized in nodules and strands with calcifications and duct-like structures.

A thick fibrous capsule surrounds odontogenic epithelium organized in cell-rich nodules of varying size containing rosettes and duct-like structures. At higher magnification, small foci of eosinophilic enamel matrix secretion (so-called tumour droplets) may be seen associated with ameloblast-like cells.
